new_symbol_range_suggestions.eta_confine_weaken: 0 <= eta_confine_weaken <= 10; observable activation when eta_confine_weaken*lambda_confine_sat*(3*Q/(pi*R**3))**n is order 0.1 to 10 across part of the sampled laminar domain

derivation_notes: The parent slip branch is retained, but the effective slip-compliance coefficient is now weakened by confinement loading through a factor 1/(1 + eta_confine_weaken*lambda_confine_sat*(3*Q/(pi*R**3))**n). This represents near-wall structuring under strong confinement reducing the marginal increase of slip with shear, while still recovering the parent when the added weakening amplitude is zero or the confinement load is small.
change_summary: The simplifying assumption that confinement only shifts slip saturation was relaxed. Confinement now also suppresses the slip-compliance strength itself at high shear-confinement loading, creating extra curvature in Delta_p versus Q that is stronger for smaller R.

assumption_audit.released_assumption: Confinement-modified near-wall structure changes only the saturation denominator of slip, not the effective slip-compliance numerator.
assumption_audit.mechanism: In strongly confined smooth-tube flow, near-wall structuring/depletion can both cap the saturation scale and reduce the marginal ability of increasing wall shear to generate further slip, so confinement acts on slip strength as well as on the slip-saturation onset.
assumption_audit.parent_reduction: The successor reduces to the parent when eta_confine_weaken = 0, or approximately when lambda_confine_sat*(3*Q/(pi*R**3))**n << 1 so the added weakening factor is near unity.

response_change.parent_relation: At fixed L, mu, n, and slip parameters, Delta_p depends on Q and R through a single smoothly saturating slip-reduction factor controlled only by the common shear scale (3*Q/(pi*R**3))**n, so the resistance reduction versus shear has one shared saturation shape across all admissible conditions.
response_change.child_relation: Retain the same shear-thinning/slip framework but relax the assumption that confinement alters slip saturation only through the saturation denominator. Instead, confinement also weakens the incremental slip compliance itself at high shear-confinement loading, producing an additional roll-off in the rate at which resistance keeps decreasing with Q at small R.
response_change.observable_effect: When Q is increased at fixed L and mu, the pressure-drop reduction from slip grows more quickly at larger R but bends over earlier for smaller R; equivalently, comparing two radii at matched nominal shear scale, the smaller tube shows less incremental slip benefit than the parent predicts once confinement-loading is order one.

evolution_contract.activation_condition: Observable when slip is active and confinement loading is not negligible: beta_slip*mu*(3*Q/(pi*R**3))**n = O(0.1-10) and lambda_confine_sat*(3*Q/(pi*R**3))**n = O(0.1-10), especially for smaller R at moderate-to-high Q within laminar flow.
evolution_contract.train_hidden_contrast: Within training, moderate changes in Q and R reveal mild radius-dependent bending of Delta_p versus Q; in holdout, extending to smaller R or larger Q strengthens this extra curvature because confinement suppresses additional slip compliance itself, not just its saturation scale.
evolution_contract.continuation_path: Recover the parent when the added confinement weakening tends to zero, e.g. vanishing new modulation amplitude or in the low-loading limit lambda_confine_sat*(3*Q/(pi*R**3))**n << 1 where the extra compliance roll-off is inactive.
evolution_contract.scientific_mechanism: In strongly confined smooth-tube flow, near-wall structuring/depletion can both cap the saturation scale and reduce the marginal ability of increasing wall shear to generate further slip, so confinement acts on slip strength as well as on slip saturation onset.
evolution_contract.difficulty_rationale: This is harder than a coefficient-only correction because the coefficient of the existing slip-compliance process now depends on the already varying confinement-loading quantity lambda_confine_sat*(3*Q/(pi*R**3))**n, changing the curvature of the Delta_p(Q,R) surface rather than just rescaling it globally.
evolution_contract.assumption_before: Confinement-modified near-wall structure changes only the saturation denominator of slip, not the effective slip-compliance numerator.
evolution_contract.assumption_after: Confinement loading weakens the effective slip-compliance numerator as well as modifying the slip-saturation denominator.
evolution_contract.parent_reduction: Setting eta_confine_weaken = 0 recovers the parent exactly; approximately the same occurs when lambda_confine_sat*(3*Q/(pi*R**3))**n is everywhere small enough that the added factor stays near unity.
evolution_contract.observable_signature: At fixed L, mu, n, beta_slip, gamma_slip_sat, kappa_confine_sat, and lambda_confine_sat, sweep Q for two radii within the laminar regime. The child predicts that the smaller-R curve loses incremental slip benefit earlier, so Delta_p bends upward relative to the parent at high shear-confinement loading, whereas the larger-R curve remains closer to the parent over the same Q range. This changes the scored Delta_p(Q,R) mapping itself, not merely an auxiliary interpretation.
evolution_contract.shortcut_blocked: A single refit of the parent parameters cannot generally reproduce both the low-loading and high-loading behavior because the parent has only one confinement action path: confinement alters the saturation denominator but leaves the slip-compliance numerator proportional to beta_slip*mu*(3*Q/(pi*R**3))**n. The child introduces an additional load-dependent attenuation of that numerator, so the rate at which slip benefit accumulates with increasing Q changes differently across radii once confinement loading reaches order one. Retuning beta_slip, gamma_slip_sat, kappa_confine_sat, or lambda_confine_sat can shift the common parent saturation shape, but cannot create this extra radius-dependent curvature change while keeping one shared parameter set across both conditions.

evolution_plan.activation_condition: Observable when slip is active and confinement loading is not negligible: beta_slip*mu*(3*Q/(pi*R**3))**n = O(0.1-10) and lambda_confine_sat*(3*Q/(pi*R**3))**n = O(0.1-10), especially for smaller R at moderate-to-high Q within laminar flow.
evolution_plan.train_hidden_contrast: Within training, moderate changes in Q and R reveal mild radius-dependent bending of Delta_p versus Q; in holdout, extending to smaller R or larger Q strengthens this extra curvature because confinement suppresses additional slip compliance itself, not just its saturation scale.
evolution_plan.continuation_path: Recover the parent when the added confinement weakening tends to zero, e.g. vanishing new modulation amplitude or in the low-loading limit lambda_confine_sat*(3*Q/(pi*R**3))**n << 1 where the extra compliance roll-off is inactive.
evolution_plan.gap_statement: The current model assumes confinement influences only where slip saturation occurs, while the magnitude of incremental slip compliance beta_slip remains unaffected by confinement once shear is specified.
evolution_plan.baseline_assumption: Confinement-modified near-wall structure changes only the saturation denominator of slip, not the effective slip-compliance numerator.
evolution_plan.scientific_mechanism: In strongly confined smooth-tube flow, near-wall structuring/depletion can both cap the saturation scale and reduce the marginal ability of increasing wall shear to generate further slip, so confinement acts on slip strength as well as on slip saturation onset.
evolution_plan.rationale: Parent response relationship: at fixed L and mu, increasing Q lowers the effective resistance through one slip-compliance branch whose numerator grows with shear and whose denominator saturates with a confinement-modified factor; all radius dependence enters through the same shear proxy (3*Q/(pi*R**3))**n, so one shared parameter set implies one common curvature pattern once plotted against that load. Proposed refinement: relax that idealization so confinement also attenuates the slip-compliance strength itself at high shear-confinement loading. Distinguishing condition: vary Q and compare two fixed radii while holding L, mu, n, beta_slip, gamma_slip_sat, kappa_confine_sat, and lambda_confine_sat common. In the child, the smaller-R case develops an earlier loss of incremental slip benefit, so Delta_p versus Q bends upward relative to the parent at high load; the larger-R case retains more of the parent-like slip reduction over the same Q range. This is a changed target mapping, not merely an auxiliary reinterpretation, because the predicted Delta_p(Q,R) surface changes directly. Admissible observability requires remaining laminar and using conditions where slip is already non-negligible and the confinement-loading factor reaches order unity; otherwise the child collapses back toward the parent and the contrast is weak.

selected_embedding_pattern.description: Make the coefficient of an existing process depend on a declared quantity.

scenario_text: A steady viscous liquid flows through a long, straight circular tube under fully developed laminar conditions. The benchmark predicts the pressure drop from independently selected flow rate, tube radius, fluid viscosity, and tube length. Density, wall roughness, and inlet details are fixed background conditions, so the response is governed only by viscous momentum transport within the tube. The sampled range remains below transition to unsteady or turbulent flow.
